dialect.detail: JMA ORCA medical receipt software (JMA standard receipt software), likely compiled with GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL on Linux. Uses COPY with REPLACING using // delimiters, INDEXED files with DYNAMIC access, no EXEC SQL/CICS.
evidence: ASSIGN to symbolic names (RECE01PARA, RECE04PARA, etc.)
ORGANIZATION IS INDEXED / ACCESS MODE IS DYNAMIC
No EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS

purpose.domain_detail: Japanese medical insurance receipt (レセプト) processing system - JMA ORCA (Open Receipt Computer Advantage). Handles medical billing receipt data editing and point calculation for Japanese national health insurance claims.
purpose.summary: This program (ORCR0030) is part of the JMA ORCA medical receipt software system. It processes and edits medical insurance receipt (レセプト) data, performing point/score calculations for various medical procedures, prescriptions, and examinations. It reads and writes indexed ISAM files (RECE02, RECE04, RECE05) containing receipt detail records and produces OCR-formatted output for insurance claim submission.

notable_features: 28 COPY statements with .INC copybooks using // REPLACING delimiter syntax
Multiple SELECT entries for same physical file with different access modes (DYNAMIC vs SEQUENTIAL)
OCR output area definitions (OCR1-AREA, OCR2-AREA) for insurance claim forms
53 CALL statements indicating heavy use of subprograms
Japanese EUC-encoded comments (latin-1 decoded, actually EUC-JP)
INDEXED files with both DYNAMIC and SEQUENTIAL access modes
No COMP-3 usage despite numeric processing
Extensive flag and index working-storage areas
verdict.notes: Comments are encoded in EUC-JP (Japanese) but decoded as latin-1, resulting in mojibake in the displayed text. The file is part of the well-known open-source JMA ORCA medical receipt system used in Japanese medical clinics. The // delimiter in COPY REPLACING is characteristic of GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL. Source is truncated at 16000 chars out of ~199KB total.
